biography.plain_text: Jeane von Oppenheim is an American art adviser and photography collector who established TransArt in Cologne. She advised museums, businesses and private collectors on exhibitions and acquisitions. Her gift of European photographs helped establish the Norton Museum of Art's photography collection, giving the Florida museum a substantial foundation for the discipline.

long_biography.plain_text:
Jeane von Oppenheim studied art history and photography before settling in Germany. At Cologne's Wallraf-Richartz Museum, she worked with the newly acquired Gruber collection to help establish a photography department. Her own collecting favoured unusual images, including less familiar work by recognised photographers, rather than simply assembling their best-known pictures.

She also developed auctions for the German AIDS Foundation. An early sale organised at her suggestion raised more than 800,000 deutsche marks. A later vintage-fashion and jewellery auction at Lempertz also supported the foundation. Her subsequent fundraising included recruiting donors and ticket buyers for opera galas that supported HIV projects in Germany and abroad.
